resources.name: Hadith collections + Japanese selection
resources.description: 36,512 hadiths — Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Muwatta Malik and the three forty-hadith collections (vocalised Arabic, English, multi-scholar gradings; the forties graded by their compilers' own notes) plus 281 hadiths with Japanese translations and explanations from HadeethEnc.com. Includes the corpus word index (word frequencies and narrator-name statistics; the app resolves a tapped word's roots itself). Includes fuKhushu's derived study layer: chain/text boundaries, Qur'an verse quotations, related narrations across the collections, the hadith-of-the-day pool and a cross-book theme map. Built by fuKhushu scripts/build_hadith_db.py.
resources.attribution: Hadith text, translations and gradings compiled from fawazahmed0/hadith-api (Unlicense), which credits sunnah.com and the per-edition translators in its References.md. Japanese selection from the Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths, HadeethEnc.com (Rowad Translation Center), reproduced verbatim under its published terms — HadeethEnc API snapshot 2026-08-03. Derived links, and grades taken from a hadith's own text where the source gives none (the forties' compilers' notes, al-Tirmidhī's verdicts, a main hadith's grades on its extra chains), by fuKhushu; verse quotations found against the Tanzil Project's Qur'an text (tanzil.net).

resources.name: Narrators and chains (isnād)
resources.description: 24,335 narrators — generation, reliability (with Ibn Ḥajar's verdict), dates, places, teachers and students — and the chains of 32,906 hadiths of the six books, matched to the library's numbering. Optional; built by fuKhushu scripts/build_hadith_narrators.py.
resources.attribution: Narrator records from the Hadith Narrators Dataset (+24K) and chains from the Hadith Dataset, both published on Kaggle by fahd09 (from muslimscholars.info and qaalarasulallah.com), as committed by the sahih-explorer project (github.com/merchantmoh-debug/sahih-explorer, MIT). Verdicts in Arabic are those the records quote from Ibn Ḥajar's Taqrīb al-Tahdhīb. Chains matched to this app's numbering by fuKhushu (scripts/build_hadith_narrators.py).

resources.name: Musnad Aḥmad & Sunan al-Dārimī
resources.description: Two more collections in vocalised Arabic (29,730 hadiths), linked to the library's narrations and verses, graded: al-Arnaʾūṭ's verdicts on the Musnad, Ḥusayn Salīm Asad's on al-Dārimī. Optional.
resources.attribution: Musnad Aḥmad and Sunan al-Dārimī from the Open-Hadith-Data project (github.com/mhashim6/Open-Hadith-Data; ODbL 1.0, contents DbCL 1.0), originally from the Islamware / Harf hadith encyclopedia, with its numbering. Gradings: Shuʿayb al-Arnaʾūṭ's verdicts on the Musnad (as appended to the Qurṭuba edition) and Ḥusayn Salīm Asad's on the Sunan (as appended to the Zamarlī–al-ʿIlmī edition), verbatim from the OpenITI corpus (Nigst, Romanov, Savant, Seydi, Verkinderen; release 2025.1.9, doi:10.5281/zenodo.17767721; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Runs of 100, the matching of those gradings to this numbering, chain/text boundaries, verse quotations and related narrations are fuKhushu's (scripts/build_hadith_books.py).

resources.name: Classical commentary (sharḥ)
resources.description: The commentary on 25,314 hadiths of seven collections — Fatḥ al-Bārī, al-Nawawī, ʿAwn al-Maʿbūd, Tuḥfat al-Aḥwadhī, al-Sindī, al-Muntaqā — verbatim. Optional.
resources.attribution: Commentary from the Open-Hadith-Data project (github.com/mhashim6/Open-Hadith-Data), made available under the Open Database License (ODbL 1.0), contents under the Database Contents License (DbCL 1.0); originally from the Islamware / Harf hadith encyclopedia. The works are identified by fuKhushu from their text; rows matched to this app's numbering by fuKhushu (scripts/build_hadith_sharh.py).
